summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -6 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Soybean meal +9.9%; weakest: Lean hogs -13.1%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.85% (-15 bp in a month), 2-year 4.61% (-7 bp); 2s10s curve +24 bp (-8 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.15% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.99 (+1.8% in a month, +5.8% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.529 (+3.3% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.644 (-0.4%); USD/MXN 19.65 (+5.1%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -6.0% in a month (+6.3% YTD); VIX 24.4. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 82.80 $/bbl (-18.0% in a month), Brent 89.96, ULSD 3.687 $/gal (-19.4%), natural gas 3.51 (+1.2%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -17.4% in a month, Shanghai Composite -2.0%, Hang Seng -1.7%, yuan +0.4% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 10 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (30%); S&P GSCI -13.1% in a month; gold -10.3%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
